questions.question: What does it mean that expectation may fail to exist?

The positive and negative parts may not balance properly
The expected value must be a probability, in every case without exception.
questions.explanation: Expectation can fail to exist when the positive and negative parts of $\sum x\,p_X(x)$ do not balance (the series is not well defined).

option_explanations: A valid PMF does sum to one; that is not the failure.

An expectation is a real number, not necessarily a probability in $[0,1]$; e.g. a fair die has $E[X]=3.5$, and a loss variable can have negative expectation. Probabilities lie in $[0,1]$, but $E[X]$ need not.
